22.25: You shall not offer bread to your God, from the hand of a stranger, nor any other thing that he would give: because they are all corrupted, and defiled: you shall not receive them.
22.26: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
22.27: When a bullock, or a sheep, or a goat, is brought forth, they shall be seven days under the udder of their dam: but the eighth day, and thenceforth, they may be offered to the Lord.
22.28: Whether it be a cow, or a sheep, they shall not be sacrificed the same day with their young ones.
22.29: If you immolate a victim for thanksgiving to the Lord, that he may be favourable,
22.30: You shall eat it the same day, there shall not any of it remain until the morning of the next day. I am the Lord.
22.31: Keep my commandments, and do them. I am the Lord.
22.32: Profane not my holy name, that I may be sanctified in the midst of the children of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctify you,
22.33: And who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might be your God: I am the Lord.

23.1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
23.2: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall call holy.
23.3: Six days shall ye do work: the seventh day, because it is the rest of the sabbath, shall be called holy. You shall do no work on that day: it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your habitations.
23.4: These also are the holy days of the Lord, which you must celebrate in their seasons.
23.5: The first month, the fourteenth day of the month at evening, is the phase of the Lord:
23.6: And the fifteenth day of the same month is the solemnity of the unleavened bread of the Lord. Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread.
23.7: The first day shall be most solemn unto you, and holy: you shall do no servile work therein:
23.8: But you shall offer sacrifice in fire to the Lord seven days. And the seventh day shall be more solemn, and more holy: and you shall do no servile work therein.
23.9: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
23.10: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall have entered into the land which I will give you, and shall reap your corn, you shall bring sheaves of ears, the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest:
23.11: Who shall lift up the shed before the Lord, the next day after the sabbath, that it may be acceptable for you, and shall sanctify it.
23.12: And on the same day that the sheaf is consecrated, a lamb without blemish of the first year shall be killed for a holocaust of the Lord.
23.13: And the libations shall be offered with it, two tenths of hour tempered with oil for a burnt offering of the Lord, and a most sweet odour: libations also of wine, the fourth part of a hin.
23.14: You shall not eat either bread, or parched corn, or frumenty of the harvest, until the day that you shall offer thereof to your God. It is a precept for ever throughout your generations, and all your dwellings.
23.15: You shall count therefore from the morrow after the sabbath, wherein you offered the sheaf of the firstfruits, seven full weeks.
23.16: Even unto the marrow after the seventh week be expired, that is to say, fifty days, and so you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord.
23.17: Out of all your dwellings, two leaves of the firstfruits, of two tenths of flour leavened, which you shall bake for the firstfruits of the Lord.
23.18: And you shall offer with the leaves seven lambs without blemish of the first year, and one calf from the herd, and two rams, and they shall be for a holocaust with their libations far a most sweet odour to the Lord.
23.19: You shall offer also a buck goat for sin, and two lambs of the first year for sacrifices of peace offerings.
23.20: And when the priest hath lifted them up with the leaves of the firstfruits before the Lord, they shall fall to his use.
23.21: And you shall call this day most solemn, and most holy. You shall do no servile work therein. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in all your dwellings and generations.
23.22: And when you reap the corn of your land, you shall not cut it to the very ground: neither shall you gather the ears that remain; but you shall leave them for the poor and for the strangers. I am the Lord your God.
23.23: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
23.24: Say to the children of Israel: The seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall keep a sabbath, a memorial, with she sound of trumpets, and it shall be called holy.
23.25: You shall do no servile work therein, and you shall offer a holocaust to the Lord.
23.26: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
23.27: Upon the tenth day of this seventh month shall be the day of atonement, it shall be most solemn, and shall be called holy: and you shall afflict your souls on that day, and shall offer a holocaust to the Lord.
23.28: You shall do no servile work in the time of this day: because it is a day of propitiation, that the Lord your God may be merciful unto you.
23.29: Every soul that is not afflicted on this day, shall perish from among his people:
23.30: And every soul that shall do any work, the same will I destroy from among his people.
23.31: You shall do no work therefore on that day: it shall be an everlasting ordinance unto you in all your generations, and dwellings.
23.32: It is a sabbath of rest, and you shell afflict your souls beginning on the ninth day of the month: from evening until evening you shall celebrate your sabbaths.
23.33: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
23.34: Say to the children of Israel: From the fifteenth day of this same seventh month, shall be kept the feast of tabernacles seven days to the Lord.
23.35: The first day shall be called most solemn and most holy: you shall do no servile work therein. And seven days you shall offer holocausts to the Lord.
23.36: The eighth day also shall be most solemn and most holy, and you shall offer holocausts to the Lord: for it is the day of assembly and congregation: you shall do no servile work therein.
23.37: These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall call most solemn and most holy, and shall offer on them oblations to the Lord, holocausts and libations according to the rite of every day,
23.38: Besides the sabbaths of the Lord, and your gifts, and those things that you offer by vow, or which you shall give to the Lord voluntarily.
23.39: So from the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you shall have gathered in all the fruits of your land, you shall celebrate the feast of the Lord seven days: on the first day and the eighth shall be a sabbath, that is a day of rest.
23.40: And you shall take to you on the first day the fruits of the fairest tree, and branches of palm trees, and boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God.
23.41: And you shall keep the solemnity thereof seven days in the year. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in your generations. In the seventh month shall you celebrate this feast.
23.42: And you shall dwell in bowers seven days: every one that is of the race of Israel, shall dwell in tabernacles:
23.43: That your posterity may know, that I made the children of Israel to dwell in tabernacles, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
23.44: And Moses spoke concerning the feasts of the Lord to the children of Israel.

24.1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
24.2: Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee the finest and dearest oil of olives, to furnish the lamps continually,
24.3: Without the veil of the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. And Aaron shall set them from evening until morning before the Lord, by a perpetual service and rite in your generations.
24.4: They shall be set upon the most pure candlestick before the Lord continually.
24.5: Thou shalt take also fine hour, and shalt bake twelve leaves thereof, two tenths shall be in every loaf :
24.6: And thou shalt set them six and six one against another upon the most clean table before the Lord:
24.7: And thou shalt put upon them the dearest frankincense, that the bread may be for a memorial of the oblation of the Lord.
24.8: Every sabbath they shall be changed before the Lord, being received of the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant:
24.9: And they shall be Aaron's and his sons', that they may eat them in the holy place: because it is most holy of the sacrifices of the Lord by a perpetual right.
24.10: And behold there went out the son of a woman of Israel, whom she had of an Egyptian, among the children of Israel, and fell at words in the camp with a man of Israel.
24.11: And when he had blasphemed the name, and had cursed it, he was brought to Moses: (now his mother was called Salumith, the daughter of Dabri, of the tribe of Dan:)
24.12: And they put him into prison, till they might know what the Lord would command.
24.13: And the Lord spoke to Moses,
24.14: Saying: Bring forth the blasphemer without the camp, and let them that heard him, put their hands upon his head, and let all the people stone him.
24.15: And thou shalt speak to the children of Israel: the man that curseth his God, shall bear his sin:
24.16: And he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, dying let him die: all the multitude shall stone him, whether he be a native or a stranger. He that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, dying let him die.
24.17: He that striketh and killeth a man, dying let him die.
24.18: He that killeth a beast, shall make it good, that is to say, shall give beast for beast.
24.19: He that giveth a blemish to any of his neighbours: as he hath done, so shall it be done to him:
24.20: Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, shall he restore. What blemish he gave, the like shall he be compelled to suffer.
24.21: He that striketh a beast, shall render another. He that striketh a man shall be punished.
24.22: Let there be equal judgment among you, whether he be a stranger, or a native that offends: because I am the Lord your God.
24.23: And Moses spoke to the children of Israel: and they brought forth him that had blasphemed, without the camp, and they stoned him. And the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses.

25.1: And the Lord spoke to Moses in mount Sinai, saying:
25.2: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall have entered into the land which I will give you, observe the rest of the sabbath to the Lord.
25.3: Six years thou shalt sow thy field and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and shalt gather the fruits thereof:
25.4: But in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath to the land, of the resting of the Lord: thou shalt not sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard.
25.5: What the ground shall bring forth of itself, thou shalt not reap: neither shalt thou gather the grapes of the firstfruits as a vintage: for it is a year of rest to the land:
25.6: But they shall be unto you for meat, to thee and to thy manservant, to thy maidservant and thy hireling, and to the strangers that sojourn with thee:
25.7: All things that grow shall be meat to thy beasts and to thy cattle.
25.8: Thou shalt also number to thee seven weeks of years, that is to say, seven times seven, which together make forty-nine years:
25.9: And thou shalt sound the trumpet in the seventh month, the tenth day of the month, in the time of the expiation in all your land.
25.10: And thou shalt sanctify the fiftieth year, and shalt proclaim remission to all the inhabitants of thy land: for it is the year of jubilee. Every man shall return to his possession, and every one shall go back to his former family:
25.11: Because it is the jubilee and the fiftieth year. You shall not sow, nor reap the things that grow in the field of their own accord, neither shall you gather the firstfruits of the vines,
25.12: Because of the sanctification of the jubilee: but as they grow you shall presently eat them.
25.13: In the year of the jubilee all shall return to their possessions.
25.14: When thou shalt sell any thing to thy neighbour, or shalt buy of him; grieve not thy brother: but thou shalt buy of him according to the number of years from the jubilee.
25.15: And he shall sell to thee according to the computation of the fruits.
25.16: The more years remain after the jubilee, the more shall the price increase: and the less time is counted, so much the less shall the purchase cost. For he shall sell to thee the time of the fruits.
25.17: Do not afflict your countrymen, but let every one fear his God: because I am the Lord your God.
25.18: Do my precepts, and keep my judgments, and fulfil them: that you may dwell in the land without any fear,
25.19: And the ground may yield you its fruits, of which you may eat your fill, fearing no mall's invasion.
25.20: But if you say: What shall we eat the seventh year, if we sow not, nor gather our fruits?
25.21: I will give you my blessing the sixth year, and it shall yield the fruits of three years:
25.22: And the eighth year you shall sow, and shall eat of the old fruits, until the ninth year: till new grow up, you shall eat the old store.
25.23: The land also shall not be sold for ever: because it is mine, and you are strangers and sojourners with me.
25.24: For which cause all the country of your possession shall be under the condition of redemption.
25.25: If thy brother being impoverished sell his little possession, and his kinsman will, he may redeem what he had sold.
25.26: But if he have no kinsman, and he himself can find the price to redeem it:
25.27: The value of the fruits shall be counted from that time when he sold it: and the overplus he shall restore to the buyer, and so shall receive his possession again.
25.28: But if his hands find not the means to repay the price, the buyer shall have what he bought, until the year of the jubilee. For in that year all that is sold shall return to the owner, and to the ancient possessor.
25.29: He that selleth a house within the walls of a city, shall have the liberty to redeem it, until one year be expired:
25.30: If he redeem it not, and the whole year be fully out, the buyer shall possess it, and his posterity for ever, and it can- not be redeemed, not even in the jubilee.
25.31: But if the house be in a village, that hath no walls, it shall be sold according to the same law as the fields: if it be not redeemed before, in the jubilee it shall return to the owner.
25.32: The houses of Levites, which are in cities, may always be redeemed:
25.33: If they be not redeemed, in the jubilee they shall all return to the owners, because the houses of the cities of the Levites are for their possessions among the children of Israel.
25.34: But let not their suburbs be sold, because it is a perpetual possession.
25.35: If thy brother be impoverished, and weak of hand, and thou receive him as a stranger and sojourner, and he live with thee,
25.36: Take not usury of him nor more than thou gavest: fear thy God, that thy brother may live with thee.
25.37: Thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor exact of him any increase of fruits.
25.38: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might give you the land of Chanaan, and might be your God.
25.39: If thy brother constrained by poverty, sell himself to thee, thou shalt not oppress him with the service of bondservants:
25.40: But he shall be as a hireling, and a sojourner: he shall work with thee until the year of the jubilee,
25.41: And afterwards he shall go out with his children, and shall return to his kindred and to the possession of his fathers,
25.42: For they are my servants, and I brought them out of the land of Egypt: let them not be sold as bondmen:
25.43: Afflict him not by might, but fear thy God.
25.44: Let your bondmen, and your bondwomen, be of the nations that are round about you.
25.45: And of the strangers that sojourn among you, or that were born of them in your land, these you shall have for servants:
25.46: And by right of inheritance shall leave them to your posterity, and shall possess them for ever. But oppress not your brethren the children of Israel by might.
25.47: If the hand of a stranger or a sojourner grow strong among you, and thy brother being impoverished sell himself to him, or to any of his race:
25.48: After the sale he may be redeemed. He that will of his brethren shall redeem him:
25.49: Either his uncle, or his uncle's son, or his kinsman, by blood, or by affinity. But if he himself be able also, he shall redeem himself,
25.50: Counting only the years from the time of his selling unto the year of the jubilee: and counting the money that he was sold for, according to the number of the years and the reckoning of a hired servant,
25.51: If there be many years that remain until the jubilee, according to them shall he also repay the price.
25.52: If few, he shall make the reckoning with him according to the number of the years, and shall repay to the buyer of what remaineth of the years,
25.53: His wages being allowed for which he served before: he shall not afflict him violently in thy sight.
25.54: And if by these means he cannot be redeemed, in the year of the jubilee he shall go out with his children.
25.55: For the children of Israel are my servants, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt.

26.1: I am the Lord your God: you shall not make to yourselves any idol or graven thing, neither shall you erect pillars, nor set up a remarkable stone in your land, to adore it: for I am the Lord your God.
26.2: Keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary: I am the Lord.
26.3: If you walk in my precepts, and keep my commandments, and do them, I will give you rein in due seasons.
26.4: And the ground shall bring forth its increase, and the trees shall be filled with fruit.
26.5: The threshing of your harvest shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing time: and you shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land without fear.
26.6: I will give peace in your coasts: you shall sleep, and there shall be none to make you afraid. I will take away evil beasts: and the sword shall not pass through your quarters.
26.7: You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you.
26.8: Five of yours shall pursue a hundred others, and a hundred of you ten thousand: your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
26.9: I will look on you, and make you increase: you shell be multiplied, and I will establish my covenant with you.
26.10: You shall eat the oldest of the old store, and, new coming on, you shall cast away the old.
26.11: I will set my tabernacle in the midst of you, and my soul shall not cast you off.
26.12: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you shall be my people.
26.13: I am the Lord your God: who have brought you out of the land of the Egyptians, that you should not serve them, and who have broken the chains of your necks, that you might go upright.
26.14: But if you will not hear me, nor do all my commandments,
26.15: If you despise my laws, and contemn my judgments so as not to do those things which are appointed by me, and to make void my covenant:
26.16: I also will do these things to you: I will quickly visit you with poverty, and burning heat, which shall waste your eyes, and consume your lives. You shall sow your seed in vain, which shall be devoured by your enemies.
26.17: I will set my face against you, and you shall fall down before your enemies, and shall be made subject to them that hate you, you shall flee when no man pursueth you.
26.18: But if you will not yet for all this obey me: I will chastise you seven times more for your sins,
26.19: And I will break the pride of your stubbornness, and I will make to you the heaven above as iron, and the earth as brass:
26.20: Your labour shall be spent in vain, the ground shall not bring forth her increase, nor the trees yield their fruit.
26.21: If you walk contrary to me, and will not hearken to me, I will bring seven times more plagues upon you for your sins:
26.22: And I will send in upon you the beasts of the held, to destroy you and your cattle, and make you few in number, and that your highways may be desolate.
26.23: And if even so you will not amend, but will walk contrary to me:
26.24: I also will walk contrary to you, and will strike you seven times for your sins.
26.25: And I will bring in upon you the sword that shall avenge my covenant. And when you shall flee into the cities, I will send the pestilence in the midst of you, and you shall be delivered into the hands of your enemies,
26.26: After I shall have broken the staff of your bread: so that ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and give it out by weight: and you shall eat, and shall not be filled.
26.27: But if you will not for all this hearken to me, but will walk against me:
26.28: I will also go against you with opposite fury, and I will chastise you with seven plagues for your sins,
26.29: So that you shall eat the flesh of your sons and of your daughters.
26.30: I will destroy your high places, and break your idols. You shall fall among the ruins of your idols, and my soul shall abhor you.
26.31: Insomuch that I will bring your cities to be a wilderness, and I will make your sanctuaries desolate, and will receive no more your sweet odours.
26.32: And I will destroy your land, and your enemies shall be astonished at it, when they shall be the inhabitants thereof.
26.33: And I will scatter you among the Gentiles, and I will draw out the sword after you, and your land shall be desert, and your cities destroyed.
26.34: Then shell the land enjoy her sabbaths all the days of her desolation: when you shall be
26.35: In the enemy's land, she shall keep a sabbath, and rest in the sabbaths of her desolation, because she did not rest in your sabbaths when you dwelt therein.
26.36: And as to them that shall remain of you I will send fear in their hearts in the countries of their enemies, the sound of a flying leaf shall terrify them, and they shall flee as it were from the sword: they shall fall, when no man pursueth them,
26.37: And they shall every one fall upon their brethren as fleeing from wars, none of you shall dare to resist your enemies.
26.38: You shall perish among the Gentiles, and an enemy's land shall consume you.
26.39: And if of them also some remain, they shall pine away in their iniquities, in the land of their enemies, and they shall be afflicted for the sins of their fathers, and their own:
26.40: Until they confess their iniquities and the iniquities of their ancestors, whereby they have transgressed me, and walked contrary unto me.
26.41: Therefore I also will walk them, and bring them into their enemies' land until their uncircumcised mind be ashamed: then shall they pray for their sins.
26.42: And I will remember my covenant, that I made with Jacob, and Isaac, and Abraham. I will remember also the land:
26.43: Which when she shall be left by them, shall enjoy her sabbaths, being desolate for them. But they shall pray for their sins, because they rejected my judgments, and despised my laws.
26.44: And yet for all that when they were in the land of their enemies, I did not cast them off altogether, neither did I so despise them that they should be quite consumed, and I should make void my covenant with them. For I am the Lord their God.
26.45: And I will remember my former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, in the sight of the Gentiles, to be their God. I am the Lord. These are the judgments, and precepts, and laws, which the Lord gave between him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.

27.1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
27.2: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The man that shall have made a vow, and promised his soul to God, shall give the price according to estimation.
27.3: If it be a man from twenty years old unto sixty years old, he shall give fifty sides of silver, after the weight of the sanctuary:
27.5: But from the fifth year until the twentieth, a man shall give twenty sicles: a woman ten.
27.6: From one month until the fifth year. for a male shall be given five sides: for a female three.
27.7: A man that is sixty years old or upward, shall give fifteen aisles: a woman ten.
27.8: If he be poor, and not able to pay tile estimation, he shall stand before tile priest: and as much as he shall value him at, and see him able to pay, so much shall he give.
27.9: But a beast that may be sacrificed to the Lord, if ally one shall vow, shall be holy,
27.10: And cannot be changed, that is to say, neither a better for a worse, nor a worse for a better. And if he shall change it: both that which was changed, and that for which it was changed, shall be consecrated to the Lord.
27.11: An unclean beast, which cannot be sacrificed to the Lord, if my man shall vow, shall be brought before the priest:
27.12: Who judging whether it be good or bad, shall set the price:
27.13: Which if he that offereth it will give, he shall add above the estimation the fifth part.
27.14: If a man shall vow his house, and sanctify it to the Lord, the priest shall consider it, whether it be good or bad, and it shall be sold according to the price, which he shall appoint.
27.15: But if he that vowed, will redeem it, he shall give the fifth part of the estimation over and above, and shall have the house.
27.16: And if he vow the field of his possession, and consecrate it to the Lord, the price shall be rated according to the measure of the seed. If the ground be sowed with thirty bushels of barley, let it be sold for fifty sides of silver.
27.17: If he vow his field immediately from the year of jubilee that is beginning, as much as it may be worth, at so much it shall be rated.

27.25: All estimation shall be made according to the side of the sanctuary. A sicle hath twenty obols.
27.26: The firstborn, which belong to the Lord, no man may sanctify and vow: whether it be bullock, or sheep, they are the Lord's.
27.27: And if it be an unclean beast, he that offereth it shall redeem it, according to thy estimation, and shall add the fifth part of the price. If he will not redeem it, it shall be sold to another for how much soever it was estimated by thee.
27.28: Any thing that is devoted to the Lord, whether it be man, or beast, or field, shall not be sold, neither may it be redeemed. Whatsoever is once consecrated shall be holy of holies to the Lord.
27.29: And any consecration that is offered by man, shall not be redeemed, but dying shall die.
27.30: All tithes of the land, whether of corn, or of the fruits of trees, are the Lord's, and are sanctified to him.

27.34: These are the precepts which the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel in mount Sinai.

The righteousness of the law is proposed in these terms,-that whosoever shall do it shall live in it; and the purpose is, that when each has discovered his own weakness, he may not by his own strength, nor by the letter of the law (which cannot be done), but by faith, conciliating the Justifier, attain, and do, and live in it. For the work in which he who does it shall live, is not done except by one who is justified. His justification, however, is obtained by faith; and concerning faith it is written, "Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring down Christ therefrom;) or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is (says he), the word of faith which we preach: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt…
quotes.source_title: ON THE SPIRIT AND THE LETTER 29.50

quotes.quote: The sabbath was given to the Jews to be observed literally, like other things, as rites symbolically signifying something deeper. A particular kind of vacation, you see, was enjoined on them. Take care to carry out what that vacation signifies. A spiritual vacation, I mean, is tranquility of heart; but tranquility of heart issues from the serenity of a good conscience. So the person who really observes the sabbath is the one who doesn't sin. This, after all, is the way the command was given to those who were commanded to observe the sabbath: "You shall perform no servile work." "Everyone who commits sin is the slave of sin."

Long before Christ it had been said, "You shall not covet"; long before it had been said, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," a phrase which, as the apostle says, expresses the fulfillment of the whole law. And as no one loves himself unless he loves God, the Lord says that the whole Law and the Prophets depend on these two commandments.

"But if a soul should sin or hear the utterance of an oath, and he himself is a witness or sees or knows about it: if he does not make it known, he too will incur sin." That is, "If he does not make it known, he will incur sin." The addition of "and" is a common expression in the Scriptures. But this particular meaning, since it is obscure, seems to need an explanation. For it seems to say that a man sins when someone swears falsely in his hearing and he knows that that man is swearing falsely and remains silent. He knows this, if he was a witness to this matter about which an oath was taken, either having seen it or having known about it. That is, in some way he knows it. Either he saw it with his own eyes or the one who swears told him. For thus he could be aware of it. But between fear of this sin and fear of the treachery of men, there often arises no small temptation. For we can…

For if Christ took away from us that very heavy yoke of many observances, so that we are not circumcised according to the flesh, we do not immolate victims of the cattle, we do not rest even from necessary works on the Sabbath, retaining the seventh in the revolution of the days, and other things of this kind; but keep them as spiritually understood, and, the symbolizing shadows being removed, are watchful in the light of those things which are signified by them; shall we therefore say, that when it is written that whoever finds another man's property of any kind that has been lost, should return it to him who has lost it, it does not pertain to us? and many other like things whereby people learn to live piously and uprightly? and especially the Decalogue itself, which is contained in those two tables of stone, apart from the carnal observance of the Sabbath, which signifies spiritual…
quotes.source_title: AGAINST TWO LETTERS OF THE PELAGIANS 3.10

quotes.quote: If we faithfully and diligently pay attention to it, brethren, everything which was promised corporally to the Jews is fulfilled spiritually in us; for all the blessings of God which they received on earth we have obtained in our souls through the grace of baptism. Therefore, with his help, let us labor with all our strength so that we may be able to receive God's blessings and avoid his curses.

Pious souls of the Lord, what the Lord admonishes us is not to be considered merely in passing, for he says, "Be holy because I am holy." Although this term properly belongs to all the Christian people, according to what blessed Peter says, "You, however, are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation," this term seems particularly to apply to all priests in a special way. In all the letters which are addressed to the Lord's priests by any men whatsoever, it is specially indicated that they are holy. Since then this term is applied to us, we ought to inquire what precisely is its meaning. It is only through Greek that the interpretation of this word holy can be discovered. For agios is the Greek for "holy," and agios has the meaning "not of the earth." Therefore if we are more solicitous for heavenly things than for those of earth, this term is not unfittingly applied to us.

"I will look with favor upon you and make you fruitful." Full of blessedness is the man upon whom God looks with favor. Do you want to understand how great is the salvation of a man upon whom the Lord looks [with favor]? Peter had once perished and at the prompting of the devil through the lips of a servant of the high priest had destroyed the consecration of his apostolic rank. But when the Lord looked at him, he was lifted up at once.

Then follow the words "and I will establish peace in your lands." What peace does God give? The peace which the world possesses? Christ says he does not give that kind of peace, for he declares, "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give to you; not as this world gives peace do I give to you." Therefore he denies that he will give the peace of the world to his disciples. Do you want to see then what peace God gives in our land? If the land is good so that it produces fruit a hundredfold, sixtyfold or thirtyfold, it will receive from God that peace which the apostle describes: "May the peace of God which surpasses all understanding guard your hearts."

"You may lie down to rest without anxiety." Moreover, Solomon says in the book of Proverbs, "When you sit down, you need not be afraid. When you lie down, your sleep will be sweet and you will not be afraid of sudden terror or of the attack of the wicked when it comes." These words he spoke concerning the just and wise man. Furthermore it is said in blessing, "You may lie down to rest without anxiety." If you are just, no one can frighten you. If you fear God, you will fear nothing else. "The just man, like a lion, feels sure of himself";19 and in the words of David, "I shall not fear the terror of the night," and so forth. He adds still further: "The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom should I fear? The Lord is my life's refuge; of whom should I be afraid?" and again, "Though an army encamp against me, my heart will not fear." Do you see the courage and constancy of the soul that…

"I will rid your country of ravenous beasts and keep war from sweeping across your land." There are many fights which pass over our land, if we do not observe the law of God and keep his commands. Let each one return to his own soul or conscience and examine himself with interior recollection. Let him see how our land, that is, our body, is oppressed at one time by the spirit of fornication, at another by anger or fury. Again it is disturbed by the darts of avarice or struck by the javelins of envy; then it is darkened by the vice of pride. In whatever way the flesh lusts against the spirit or the spirit against the flesh, our land is agitated by exceedingly dangerous battles. Therefore, if a man observes the divine commands, by the Holy Ghost brings his body into subjection, keeps God's precepts and fulfills them, he suffers this fight and war less or endures them in such a way that he…

"Five of you will put a hundred to flight." Who are those five who can pursue a hundred? The number five is applied to both the praiseworthy and the culpable, for there were five wise virgins and five foolish; so also the number one hundred can be accepted in either way. Therefore if we belong to the five laudable ones, that is, the five wise virgins, we pursue one hundred of the foolish. If we fight wisely in matters of God's Word, if we discuss the law of the Lord prudently, we convince and put to flight a multitude of unbelievers. Similarly the number one hundred indicates both the faithful and the unfaithful. Under that number of years Abraham is recorded to have believed in God and been justified, while "the sinner of a hundred years shall be thought accursed." Now here a hundred unfaithful souls are put to flight by five wise men. Again, a hundred just men, who are so designated…

"Your foes will be cut down by your sword." Who they are we mentioned above, but let us find out by what sword they are said to fall. The apostle Paul teaches us what this sword is when he says, "For the Word of God is living and efficient and keener than every two-edged sword and extending even to the joints of soul and spirit, of the members also and the marrow, and a discerner of the thoughts and intentions of the heart." This is the sword at whose edge our enemies will fall. For it is the Word of God which casts down all enemies and puts them under its feet, so that the whole world becomes subject to God. Do you wish to learn from still another epistle of Paul that the sword with which spiritual enemies are overcome is the Word of God? Listen to him as he provides arms for the soldiers of Christ: "Take unto you the helmet of salvation and the sword of the spirit, that is, the Word…

"On the days of your solemn feasts you shall mortify yourselves." Why did he say this? Because fasts and vigils and holy mortifications afflict bodies that are humbled, but they purify hearts that have been defiled. They may take strength away from limbs, but they add a bright sheen to conscience. Sins of pleasure are redeemed by bodily weariness while the physical delights of dissipation are punished by the distresses of a hard cross. Thus by present mortification the sentence of future death is suspended.

I do not consider this as a material blessing, as though the man who observes God's law will obtain that common bread in abundance. Why not? Do not wicked sinners also eat bread, not only in abundance but even in luxury? Therefore let us look rather to him who says, "I am the living bread that has come down from heaven." And "he who eats this bread shall live forever." As we notice that he who said this is the word with which our soul is fed, we realize of what bread it was said by God in blessing that: "You will have food to eat in abundance." Solomon proclaims something similar concerning the just man, when he says in the book of Proverbs, "When the just man eats, his hunger is appeased, but the souls of the wicked suffer want." If this is understood only according to the letter, it seems utterly false, for the souls of the wicked eat more greedily and strive for satiety, while the…

The wicked man is never secure but is always disturbed and wavering. He is tossed about by every wind of doctrine to deceitful error, by the craft of men. However, the just man who observes God's law dwells in security on his land, because he governs his body in fear of God and brings it into subjection. His understanding is firm when he says to God, "Strengthen me according to your words, O Lord." Strengthened, secure and well rooted, he dwells on the earth, founded in faith. His house is not built upon sand but is established on solid ground.

"You will rout your enemies." Of what enemies do we speak, except the devil himself and his angels? We rout them not only by driving them from our own hearts, but we repel them far away from others whom they disturb or attack or overcome. We do this by our advice or reproof or prayer, if we preserve the divine precepts. Thus through death the enemy falls in our sight. Whose death? I think it is ours when we mortify our members which are on earth, namely, fornication and impurity. If we bring this death to our members, that is, to our concupiscences and sins, our enemies, the devil and his angels, will fall in our sight. How will they fall in your sight? If you are just, injustice falls at sight of you; if chaste, lust falls; if devout, you kill the spirit of impiety.

A first baptism was that of the flood [of Noah] that cut away of sin. A second was that by the [Red] Sea and the cloud, for the cloud is a symbol of the Spirit, while the sea is a symbol of the water. A third is that of the [Levitical] law, for every unclean person washed himself with water and also washed his garments and thus entered into the camp. A fourth is that of John, which was an introductory baptism leading those thus baptized to penance, so that they might believe in Christ.

For from the beginning "the spirit of God moved over the waters," and over and again Scripture testifies to the fact that water is purifying. It was with water that God washed away the sin of the world in the time of Noah. It was with water that every one who was unclean was purified in accordance with the law, and even their garments were washed with water.

He himself says, "Be holy, for I am holy," that is to say, choose me and keep away from what displeases me. Do what I love; love what I do. If what I order seems difficult, come back to me who ordered it, so that from where the command was given help might be offered. I who furnished the desire will not refuse support. Fast from contradiction, abstain from opposition. Let me be your food and drink. None desire in vain what is mine, for those who stretch out toward me seek me because I first sought them.

"And I will set my tabernacle among you". If we have these things in us which were said above, if, the "old man" having been cast off, our heart has been renewed, God comes to us and dwells in us, He who said: "and I will set my tabernacle among you, and my soul shall not abominate you". "The soul of God" will not "abominate" us, if we observe the things which are written. Yet I should wish to inquire what is "the soul of God". Shall we perhaps suppose that God has a soul as a man has? It is absurd to think this of God. But I dare and say that the soul of God is Christ. For just as Christ is "the Word" of God and "the wisdom of God and the power of God", so also He is the soul of God. And in this manner it is said: "my soul shall not abominate you", that is, my Son, but "I will walk among you".

It does not seem to me that God promises this, that He will walk in the land of the Jews, but that, if anyone should deserve to be of so pure a heart as to be capable of God, in him God says that He "walks". — "And you shall be to me a people".

After these things, now the matters which are recounted in what follows are not without a certain question, concerning which, though many have inquired, not many have been able to explain. But if you help me with your prayers, we too will attempt to bring forward into the midst what the Lord shall grant. "A man, a man," it says, "if he shall curse God, shall receive sin; but he who names the name of the Lord, let him die the death." What is this? He who "shall curse God" does not have the penalty of death, but "he who shall name the name of the Lord"? Is it not far more grievous to "curse God" than to "name" Him, although he is said to have named Him in vain? And how is it that he who "curses" only takes on sin, but he who "names" is punished "with death"? These, then, are the things which in this passage are wont to raise a question, which to those ignorant of the sense of the…

For we eat with blessing the old things, the prophetic words and the old things of the old things, the words of the law. And, when the new and evangelical words came, living according to the gospel, we bring forth the old things of the letter from before the new. He sets his tabernacle in us, fulfilling the promise which he spoke, "I will dwell among them and walk in them."
quotes.source_title: COMMENTARY ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 10.15

quotes.quote: "I will establish", He says, "my covenant with you. And you shall eat the old things and the old of the old, and you shall cast out the old from before the face of the new". How do we "cast out the old from before the face of the new"? "The old" things: "we had the law and the prophets"; but "the old of the old" are those things which were before the law, from the beginning, when the world was made. There came the new Gospels, there came also the Apostles. From before the face of these we cast out "the old things". How do we cast them out? We cast out the law according to the letter, that we may establish the law according to the spirit. We can also say in this manner: before the man came "from heaven" and the "heavenly man" was born, we were all "earthly" and "bore the image of the earthly"; but when there came "the new man, who was created according to God", we cast out "from before…

But let us see what is the first blessing for those who have fulfilled the things which are commanded. "I will give", He says, "you rain in its season". Therefore let us first say to the Jews and to those who suppose these things are to be understood simply or bodily: if this "rain" is given as a reward for labors to those who "keep the commandments", how is it that also to those who do not keep the commandments one and the same "rain" is given in its seasons, and the whole world makes use of the common rains given by God? For "He rains upon the just and the unjust". But if "rain" is given "to the just and the unjust", it will not be an exceptional reward for those who have kept the commandments. See therefore that, even if the Jews do not acquiesce in the words of Jesus our Lord, yet you, who are reckoned by His name and are called a Christian, ought to believe Him when He says that…

"And flaying," it says, "the whole burnt offering, they shall divide it limb by limb, and the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire upon the altar, and shall pile up wood on the fire; and the sons of Aaron the priest shall lay on the divided limbs and the head and the fat and the wood which are upon the altar. But the entrails and the feet they shall wash with water, and the priest shall lay all upon the altar; it is a victim and a sacrifice, an odor of sweetness to the Lord." How the flesh of the Word of God, which here is named a "calf," is flayed, and how it is divided "limb by limb" by the priests, is worth observing. I think that that priest strips off the hide of the "calf" offered as a "whole burnt offering" and draws off the skin by which its limbs are covered, who strips from the Word of God the veil of the letter and lays bare its inner parts, which are the limbs of…

"This is," it says, "the law of the sacrifice of the peace offering, which they shall offer to the Lord. If indeed he offers it for a thanksgiving, he shall also bring to the sacrifice loaves of thanksgiving made of fine flour in oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and fine meal mingled with oil. Upon leavened loaves he shall offer his gifts, because it is the sacrifice of thanksgiving of his peace offering. And he shall offer of it one from all his gifts as a separation to the Lord; it shall belong to the priest who pours out the blood of the peace offering; and the flesh of the sacrifice of thanksgiving of the peace offering, it shall be his; and on the day on which the gift is offered, they shall eat it, and they shall not leave any of it until the morning". This sacrifice, which is called "the peace offering", it divides into two parts, and one indeed it names of…

But our Lord Jesus Christ alone, "who knows no sin", "was defiled neither in father nor in mother" and "did not go out from the holy places". There were indeed some things to be set before the Jews in the passages above, to which they could not respond, but omitting those, what do they for the present tell us on this discourse, either they themselves or those who wish the law to be understood according to their sense: if these things are not referred to our high priest and Savior, how will it be proved according to the letter that "the great priest did not go out from the holy places", who nevertheless even took a wife, as is said below, "a virgin of his own kindred"? If "he does not go out from the holy places", if he goes forth nowhere, how or for what uses is he commanded to "take a wife"? For it must not be supposed that he could remain within the holy places with a wife. But let…

So then he washed him and clothed him. With what garment? "With a tunic," he says, "and he girded him with the girdle, and again he clothed him with the ankle-length tunic", or, as we read elsewhere, "the inner tunic". With two tunics, as I see, the high priest is clothed through Moses. But what do we make of the fact that Jesus forbade his priests, our Apostles, to use two tunics? And we had said that Moses and Jesus, that is, the law and the gospels, are consonant with one another. Someone might perhaps be able to say that what Jesus commanded, that two tunics are not to be had, is not contrary to the law, but more perfect than the law, just as when the law forbids murder, but Jesus cuts away even anger, and when the law prohibits adultery, Jesus cuts off even the concupiscence of the heart. So then it will seem that there the high priest was clothed with two tunics, and here the…

Now the sixth and last kind of leprosy is set down, which "comes in baldness or forehead-baldness"; which things, as far as they are in themselves, are clean. For thus also the law says: "If any one's," it says, "hairs of the head have fallen off, he is bald, he is clean. But if they have fallen off from his forehead, he is forehead-bald, he is clean." And these things are suitably referred to the soul, so that, when it casts off and lays aside those things which are dead by their own nature, it is said to be clean. But after this, if those things which had first been purified shall be seen to sprout up again, filthier and lower than the dignity of purity requires, they will render the soul unclean and leprous.

In bodily contests certain grades and distinctions of the several ranks are customarily observed, so that each one may be rewarded with the prize of victory according to the quality of the struggle. For instance, if someone should have a contest among boys, or among youths, or among men, what observance ought to be kept for each rank, what may be done and what may not be done, and what rule of the contest is to be guarded, and what palm of reward the victor deserves after these things—all this is nonetheless provided for by the very laws of the games. So now too Almighty God, appointing for mortals in this world a contest of observing His law, after He had handed down very many things to be observed and had prescribed what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fittingly, at the very end, in the book of Leviticus, in which it is laid down concerning each of the several…

But let us now see what is the opening of the blessings in Leviticus. "If", He says, "you walk in my precepts, and keep my commandments and do them". There are three things which He says: "one must walk in the precepts, one must keep the commandments and do the things which are commanded". Whence it seems to me that a precept is, for instance, when it is enjoined that he who has not kept the sabbath "be stoned by the whole synagogue", or "he who has cursed God, that he be destroyed with stones", and any such things that are enjoined. But that commandments are those by which it is enjoined, for instance, that tithes be offered to the Levites, or "to appear before the Lord three times in the year", or "not to appear empty in the sight of the Lord". "To keep" therefore is "the commandment" to understand or to attend to the things which are enjoined; but "to do" is "the commandment" to…

"And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering; in the place where the whole burnt offerings are slaughtered, they shall also slay that which is for sin before the Lord; they are the holy of holies. The priest who offers it shall eat it; it shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the tabernacle of testimony. Everyone who touches its flesh shall be sanctified; and whoever has been sprinkled with its blood upon a garment, whatever has been sprinkled, that too shall be washed in a holy place. And the earthen vessel in which it has been cooked shall be broken; but if it has been cooked in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it and rinse it with water. Every male of the priests shall eat of these; they are the holy of holies to the Lord. And all the things that are for sin, from whose blood some has been brought into the…

For "on account of sins not voluntary" it is in general the "soul" that is commanded to offer, but after this the text proceeds through diverse and various persons; and it is commanded that, "if indeed it be the high priest who has transgressed and offers a sacrifice for sin, he should offer a bull-calf" as a whole burnt offering, but not by that same rite by which he offered the one for an offering. For of this one he shall place upon the altar of the whole burnt offerings "the fat and the two kidneys with their fat, and the fat that covers the inner parts", only these. "Of its blood" too, "dipping his finger, he sprinkles seven times before the Lord, and anoints from it the horns of the altar of incense. But the rest of the flesh, with the hide and the entrails and the dung, he commands to be burned with fire outside the camp, in a clean place". It must indeed be observed that in the…

But these things have been said in general; now, however, they are divided by kinds. "If the high priest", it says, "who has been anointed, should sin, so as to make the people sin, he shall offer for his own sin a bull-calf from the oxen, without blemish, to the Lord". Both terror and mercy are displayed together in the divine laws. Is nothing, then, after all, safe — not even the high priest? And what high priest? The very one who has been anointed, the very one who kindles the divine altars with the sacred fires, who immolates offerings and peace offerings to God; who intervenes as a certain mediating re-propitiator between God and men — not even he, I say, remains immune from the contagion of sin. But see the mercy of God, and know it more fully from Paul's teaching. For he himself, writing to the Hebrews, says: "for every high priest taken from among men is appointed for men to…

But in the moral sense this high priest can be seen as that faculty of piety and religion which within us performs, as it were, a certain priesthood, through the prayers and supplications that we pour out to God. If this transgress in anything, it forthwith "makes sin" the whole people of good acts that is within us. For we do nothing of a right work when the guiding sense of good works has declined into what is depraved; and therefore for the amending of this, not any victim whatever, but the sacrifice of "the fatted calf" itself is required. Likewise too the fault of the synagogue — that is, the amending of all the virtues that are within us — is repaired not otherwise than by the mortification of Christ.

Yet he is not immediately permitted to enter his own house, but it is said that he "remain outside his own house for seven days, and shave every hair of his head and beard and eyebrows"; as though it had not been enough that he had first "shaved every hair," now it is added that he "shave every hair of his head and beard and eyebrows." For the same thing seemed to have been said in that he had said "every hair was to be shaved." But this repetition does not seem to me to be empty. For he wills, after the sinner shall have been made clean, after he shall have received through repentance the remission of sins, to admonish him concerning the purgation "of the head and of the beard and of the eyebrows," as if he were saying to him: "Behold, thou art now made whole," see that thou contract no further guilt of the head. For "the sin of the head" is to think otherwise concerning the divine…

Who is there who has grasped the mind of Christ so well that he knows the meaning of the seventh year of freedom of Hebrew slaves and the remission of debts and the intermission of the cultivation of the holy land? Over and above the feast of every seventh year is the feast called the jubilee. No one can ever come near divining its precise meaning or the true import of the prescriptions enjoined by it, except him who knows the Father's will and his disposition for every age according to "his incomprehensible judgments and unsearchable ways."

"And the Lord spoke," it says, "to Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: You shall not eat any fat of oxen and of sheep and of goats. And the fat of carrion, and of what is caught from a wild beast, shall not be for any work, and shall not be eaten as food. Everyone who eats the fat of the cattle from which you offer from them a victim to the Lord, that soul shall perish from his people. And you shall not eat any blood in all your habitation, from cattle and from birds. Every soul, whatever it be, that eats blood, that soul shall perish from his people". The lawgiver refuses that the "fats" of those animals which are offered in the sacrifices, and of certain others, be eaten or held in use; but he forbids the "blood" of any flesh to be eaten. In the foregoing, treating the mystical passage where the "calf" was given as a whole burnt offering "for sin" and the fats were…

"And there shall be placed", it says, "upon the row clean frankincense". The kind of frankincense holds the form of prayers. It is fitting, therefore, to join to the loaves of faith the vigilance and purity of prayers. And prayer is pure, as the Apostle says: "lifting up pure hands without wrath and dispute". At the same time the sweetness of the odor also causes to be fulfilled that which is written: "let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight". If anyone, therefore, offers prayers indeed to God, but does not have a conscience clean from evil works, this man seems indeed to "place frankincense" upon the loaves, but not entirely "clean" frankincense. For if all frankincense were "clean", Scripture would surely not have added that "clean frankincense" be "placed before the Lord" upon the shewbread. For do not suppose that almighty God commanded this and sanctioned it by law, that…

"And I will look upon you and increase you". Full of beatitude is this very thing, if "God look upon" anyone. Do you wish to see, if "the Lord look upon" a man, how great is salvation? Peter had once almost perished and, by the devil breathing through the mouth of "the maidservant of the high priest", had been snatched from the consecration of the apostolic number; but when "Jesus only looked upon him", when He turned toward him the countenance of a placid face, at once, returning into himself and recalling his foot slipped from the precipice, "he wept", it says, "most bitterly", and thus, looked upon by God, by weeping he recovered his place, which by denying he had lost. — "I will look", therefore, He says, "upon you, and increase you". As if the sun should look upon a crop and bring forth its fruits—which surely, if it had not looked upon it, would have remained fruitless—so God,…

But also "a harlot he shall not take". What is a "harlot" soul? One that receives to itself "lovers", of whom the prophet says: "you have played the harlot after your lovers". Who are these "lovers" who enter in to the harlot soul, except the adverse powers and demons, who conceive desire of her beauty? For the soul was created beautiful by God and exceedingly comely. Hear how God himself says: "let us make man according to our image and likeness". See of what comeliness, of what beauty the soul is; it has the "image and likeness" of God. When the adverse powers behold this beauty, that is, "the devil and his angels", they covet its form; and because they cannot become its bridegrooms, they desire to play the harlot with it. If therefore you receive, O man, into the bedchamber of your soul the adulterer "devil", your soul has played the harlot with the devil. If you receive "his…

After these things: "and the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: And speak to the sons of Israel, saying: He who offers a sacrifice of his peace offering to the Lord shall offer his gift to the Lord from the sacrifice of his peace offering. His hands shall offer the victim to the Lord: the fat which is upon the little breast and the lobe of the liver, he shall offer them so that they be set as a gift before the Lord. And the priest shall place the fat which is upon the little breast upon the altar, and the little breast shall be Aaron's and his sons'. And the right arm you shall give as a separation to the priest from your peace offerings. He who offers the blood of the peace offering and the fat from the sons of Aaron, to him shall the right arm be as a portion. For the little breast of the placing and the arm of the taking-away I have received from the sons of Israel from your peace…

Perhaps in another way also "the man ready" and clean, who "leads away that one whose lot has come, into the wilderness", and by that very act by which he leads him out, as one who has touched something unclean, is said to "wash his garments" at evening and to be clean — perhaps even our Lord and Savior himself may be understood, in that part in which he took on the "garments" of our nature, that is, of flesh and blood, which he "washed at evening"; on account of which also the prophet had long ago said of him: "and I saw Jesus the great priest, clothed in filthy garments, and the devil standing at his right hand, that he might contradict him." Therefore he "washed his robe in wine" — that is, in his own blood — "at evening", and was made "clean". And thence perhaps it was that after the resurrection he said to Mary, who wished to hold his feet: "do not touch me." But do you wish to see…

But when the priest shall have seen him, he commands that "there be taken two living hens for him who is being made clean, and cedar wood and twisted scarlet and hyssop." It seems to me that here too these "two hens" have a certain likeness of the two goats, of which one is offered to the Lord and the other is sent forth "into the wilderness"; for so here also, of the two hens, one is immolated and the other is let go "into the field." He, then, who is being purged of leprosy gives here too some part which is cast away "into the wilderness"; but the other part is offered to the Lord for him. Yet not yet does this one, who is being purged of leprosy and offers the hens, offer at the altar even that very hen which is offered for him to the Lord, as "turtledoves or doves." For not yet "on the same day" is he who is being purged of leprosy made worthy of the divine altar. On account of…

Thereupon the order of the sacrifices is directed to the offering of victims for sins, in which it is said a second time: "the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: whatever soul shall sin before the Lord unwillingly". Rightly does it say "soul" of the one whom it describes as sinning; for it would not have called it spirit, of which it would say that it would sin; but neither would it call this one a man, in whom, with sin intervening, the "image of God" in no way stands firm. It is not, then, the spirit that sins; for "the fruit of the spirit" — as the Apostle describes — "is love, joy, peace, patience", and the rest like these, which are also called "the fruits of life". Finally, elsewhere too he says: "he who sows in the flesh shall from the flesh reap corruption; and he who sows in the spirit shall from the spirit reap eternal life". Since, then, there is one who sows and another in whom it…

"He shall be unclean," it says, "and shall sit separated outside, his dwelling shall be outside the camp." It is clear that every "unclean" one is cast out from the assembly of the good and separated from the company and camps of the saints; and therefore it says that: "his dwelling shall be outside the camp."

From this now, generally, concerning every leper in whom there shall have been "the contagion of leprosy" and it shall appear "lower than the rest of the skin" — for every vice of the soul is lower than its remaining virtues — the law, which "is spiritual," decrees certain such things: "Let his garments," it says, "be unstitched, and his head uncovered, and his mouth covered over." By which it designates that he who is leprous in soul, that is, who is fixed fast with sins, ought not to sew coverings upon himself and to cover over the baseness of sin. For just as he whose "garments are unstitched" bears the baseness of his body naked and uncovered, so ought he who is hedged about with some sins to cover his evils and disgraceful deeds with no sewn-on words, with no veils of excuses; so that he may not become "a whited sepulchre, which outwardly indeed appears beautiful to men, but within…

The fourth was the law, where it is said that "if in the skin there comes a burning of fire," and after these things, "when the burning has been healed, it itself becomes shining and white with redness, or certainly whitish, and the appearance of it is lower than the rest of the skin": and this he says is "the leprosy which has flowered in the burning." See, then, whether "a burning" is not in every soul whatsoever that receives "the fiery darts of the evil one"; or whether everyone who burns in carnal love is not "scorched by fire." These, then, are the "burnings" and kindlings of "fire." But also he suffers "a burning" who is set ablaze by desire of human glory, and who is inflamed by the heats of anger or fury. But if perchance the soul be cured of these wounds through faith, and after health received, despising him who said: "Behold, thou art now made whole, sin no more, lest…

But note also this, how, whereas above he had said: "This is the law of the leper; on the day on which he shall have been made clean," now he adds to all these things and says: "and he shall be clean." For if the leprosy having once been cast off he "has been made clean," how shall he still "be clean"? But see that, even if anyone be made clean from sin and be no longer in the act of sin, nevertheless the very traces of the crime committed need purification, both that which we have expounded and, no less, others which are commanded in what follows. For we have observed that to this — that it is written concerning leprosy: "on the day on which he shall have been made clean" — after these things, among the other things which are commanded, it is said a third time: "and he shall be clean," and again at the last it is written: "and he shall be cleansed." Whence it seems to me that there are…

And first I should like to see what this distinction is: that of one it says that "a man" offers, of another that "a soul" offers, of another "the high priest", of another "the synagogue", of another "one soul from the people of the land". And I think indeed that "a man" is to be understood as one who, made "to the image and likeness" of God, lives rationally. This man, then, offers to God an offering — a "bull-calf", when he has overcome the pride of the flesh; a "sheep", when he has corrected the irrational and foolish motions; a "kid", when he has conquered wantonness. He offers too "a pair of turtledoves", when he has not been alone, but has joined his mind to the Word of God as to a true spouse, just as this kind of bird is said to keep a single and chaste marriage. He offers too "two young pigeons", when he too has understood the mystery in which "the eyes of the bride" are said…

After these things: "and every sacrifice," it says, "made in oil or not made shall belong to all the sons of Aaron, to each equally". What sacrifice is "made in oil" or which is that "not made in oil"? The "sacrifice of the peace offering" is commanded to be made "in oil", as we have already said above. But the "sacrifice for sin" is not made "in oil"; for it says: "he shall not put oil upon it, since it is for sin". That, then, which is "for sin", neither is the "oil of gladness" put upon it nor the incense of sweetness; for concerning those who sin the Apostle says: "and I shall mourn those who have sinned before and have not done penance". Nor is there in it the "odor of sweetness", because from the person of the sinner it is said: "my scars have rotted and are corrupted". These things for the time being have been observed by us concerning the earlier chapter, where the law of the…

The troubling utterance is the following: "The soul of all flesh is the blood" — behold an extremely difficult passage, which has shaken those who did not understand it! … According to my measure of understanding, and with prayer for help in the knowledge of the Divine utterances … I have observed that incorporeal things are given the same names as corporeal things, and thus corporeal things are related to the outer man, while those bearing the same names as the corporeal are related to the inner man. Scripture says that in man there are two. … Therefore in each of us there are two men. Why does the Holy Scripture say that the soul of all flesh is the blood? This is a difficult question. Just as the outer man is homonymous with the inner one, so also with respect to the parts of the body. One may say that each part of the body of the outer man is homonymous with the corresponding part…

Let us see after these things what the things are which the high priest does: "and he shall take" it says "a censer full of coals of fire from the altar which is before the Lord". We read also in Isaiah that the prophet is purged by fire through "one of the seraphim, which was sent to him, when it took with tongs one coal from those which were upon the altar, and touched the lips of the prophet and said": "behold, I have taken away your iniquities". To me these things seem to be mystical and to indicate this, that to each one, according to that in which he sins, if he is worthy to be purified, coals are applied to his members. For since the prophet here says: "I have unclean lips, and I dwell also in the midst of a people having unclean lips", therefore the "coal taken up with the tongs" by the seraph purges his lips, in which alone he professes himself not to be clean. From which it is…

"And he shall take" it says "a censer full of coals". Not all are purged by that fire which is taken "from the altar". Aaron is purged by that fire, and Isaiah, and any who are like them; but others, who are not such, among whom I reckon even myself, we shall be purged by another fire — I fear lest by that of which it is written: "a river of fire ran before him". That "fire" is not "from the altar". The fire which is "from the altar" is the fire of the Lord; but that which is outside the altar is not the Lord's, but is the proper fire of each one of those who sin, of which it is said: "their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be extinguished". That "fire" therefore is of those very ones who kindled it, as also elsewhere it is written: "walk in your fire and in the flame which you have kindled for yourselves". But to Isaiah not his own fire is applied, but the fire of the…

Therefore the high priest "takes a censer full of coals of fire from the altar which is before the Lord, and fills his hand with the fine incense of composition and carries it into the interior of the veil". Let us understand first what the history designates, and then let us inquire what the spiritual sense holds. Twofold is the house of the tabernacle of testimony or of the temple of the Lord. The first is that in which is the "altar of the whole burnt offerings", which is stirred up with perpetual fires, in which house it is lawful for the priests alone to stand and to celebrate the rites and ministries of the sacrifices, and to neither the Levites nor anyone else besides is access granted. But the second house is the interior one, separated from this only by a "veil". Within which veil are the "ark of the testament" and the "propitiatory", upon which the "two cherubim" are set, and…

But let us now see what those things are which are set forth in the law. "And the Lord spoke," it says, "to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering" and the rest which have been read in the present passage. And I remember that we have already said before that the law is not always given to the same persons, but one thing indeed is said to the sons of Israel, another to the sons of Aaron, and yet another, as we observed some time ago, to Moses and Aaron. There is also another law which is given to Moses alone, so that not even Aaron is made a partaker of that law. Who has been so illumined by God with the gift of knowledge as to be able to discourse fully and clearly on the distinctions and diversities of each of these? For we find in what follows a command of the Lord given to Moses alone, and it is ordered that "the little breast of the…

And after, according to those things which were said above, the victims are offered for purification, he applies, it says, also "the cyathus of oil" and separates it "before the Lord." "And the priest," it says, "shall take of the blood, and shall put it upon the tip of his right ear and upon the extremity of his right hand and upon the extremity of his right foot." And after these things, it says, "the priest shall take" not the cyathus of oil itself, but "of" it, and "shall pour it out," it says, "into his own left hand, and the priest shall dip his finger in the oil which is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle it seven times before the Lord"; and again: "of that which remains in his left hand, he shall put it upon the right ear of him who is being purified, and upon the extremity of his right hand and upon the extremity of his right foot"; and after these things: "that which shall…

Rightly therefore to a soul of this kind it is said in the blessings: "and you shall dwell secure upon your land; and I will give peace upon your land". What "peace does" God "give"? That which the world has? Christ denies that He gives this. For He says: "my peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you; not as this world gives peace, do I also give to you". He denies therefore that He gives "the peace of the world" to His disciples, because elsewhere too He says: "do you think that I came to send peace on the earth? I came not to send peace, but a sword". Do you wish then to see what "peace God gives upon our land"? If the land be that "good" one which "bears fruit a hundredfold or sixtyfold or thirtyfold", it will receive from God that "peace" which the Apostle speaks of: "but the peace of God, which surpasses every mind, shall guard your hearts and your understandings". This then is…

But let us see how these "twelve loaves" are set forth: "two rows", it says, "six loaves in one row". Do you suppose this division is idle? Why is it that the number twelve is again divided into six? For the number six has a certain kinship with this world; for in six days this visible world was made. Two orders, therefore, are held in this world, that is, two peoples, who guard the faith of the Father and the Son in one church as it were upon "one clean table".

"I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, when you were servants, and broke the yoke of your bond". Truly "He brought us out of the house of servitude", for "we were servants" of sin, because: "everyone who sins is a servant of sin". And "He broke the bond of our yoke, the yoke" which he had imposed upon our necks who had "led us into captivity" and bound us with the bonds of sins. "He broke", therefore, the "bond" of sin and shook off the "yoke" of our captivity, our Lord Jesus Christ, and imposed upon us His own sweet yoke of faith and charity and hope and of all sanctity. To Him be glory unto the eternal ages of ages! Amen.

"And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue many thousands". Who are those "five" who can "pursue a hundred"? The number "five" is set both among the praiseworthy and among the culpable. There are "five wise virgins" and "five foolish". So therefore also the number of a hundred can be taken to either part. If then we be of the five praiseworthy, that is, of the five wise, we shall pursue a hundred foolish. For if we fight wisely and provably in the word of God, if we discourse prudently concerning the law of the Lord, we shall convince and put to flight a multitude of the unfaithful. For just as the number five indicates both the wise and the foolish, so also the number of a hundred indicates both the faithful and the unfaithful. For under the number of a hundred years Abraham is described as having believed God and been justified, and "the sinner who dies…

But as to what it says: "it shall be eaten within the day, nor shall it be left over of it until the morning", let us compare it with the other sacrifices and let us see what the reason is that in this peace sacrifice indeed it commanded "the things that are offered" to be "eaten on the same day", but in another sacrifice it allows them to be kept even to the second day and up to the third, but on the third day the things that remain over to be already delivered to the fire, lest they defile the one who offers. What, then, this difference may hold, let us see. But truly we need the help of God, who may deign to cut away all the "fats covering" our "inward parts" and to remove every veil of grosser sense, so that we may be able to perceive these things according to that which is said to be commanded by God. Let us therefore compare the divine Scripture itself with itself, and let us…

In the second place, the oblation "of the first fruits", that is, of the beginnings of the produce, is commanded. And this, if you remember well, the law commands to be done on the day of Pentecost. In which a "shadow" plainly was given to them, but for us the truth was reserved. For on the day of Pentecost, when the sacrifice of prayers had been offered, the Church received the first fruits of the coming "Holy Spirit" of the Apostles. And truly these were fresh, because it was new; whence they were even said to be "filled with new wine". "Roasted with fire". For fiery tongues settled upon each one. "And broken in the middle". For they were broken in the middle, when the letter was separated from the spirit. "And well cleansed". For the presence of the Holy Spirit cleanses all filth, granting remission of sins. The oil of mercy too is poured into this sacrifice, and the frankincense of…

Not without cause is a pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons, taken in the sacrifices: for they are of equal worth, and it is never said separately, a pair only of pigeons, but a pair of turtledoves, and two young pigeons. The dove is the Holy Spirit. But the Holy Spirit, when he speaks of great and more hidden mysteries, which many cannot receive, is signified by the name of the turtledove — that is, of that bird which dwells always on the ridges of the mountains and on the tops of the trees; but in the valleys, and in the things which reach even to men, the dove is taken.
quotes.source_title: HOMILIES ON THE SONG OF SONGS, HOMILY 2

quotes.quote: It will now be a great task to pursue the diversities of victims and the rites and varieties of sacrifices, and one belonging to a work far other than that discourse which the common crowd receives in the general assembly. But that we may seem to touch upon some things in passing: almost every victim, indeed, which is offered has something of the form and image of Christ. For every victim is recapitulated in him, so much so that, after "he himself was offered", all the victims ceased which had preceded him in type and "shadow"; concerning which, as far as we could, we showed in what went before how the bull-calf offered by the high priest, whether as an offering or "for sin", held his form. But the "fat", which is offered in the offering, "covering the inward parts" and clinging to the kidneys, can be understood as that holy soul of his which veiled the "inward parts", that is, the…

After this it speaks of the peace (salutary) offerings, which are offered from animals, that is, from "oxen" or "goats and sheep"; and nothing beyond these is admitted for immolation — not even the birds, which above had been admitted among the offerings to be offered.
